text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has no verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Visit of Pope John Paul II to Bosnia-Herzegovina is a comfirmation of its statehood, a boost to its reintegration, multi-confessionalism and multi-culturalism, daily says in commentary.

- Croatian foreign affairs minister, Mate Granic, visits Sarajevo to attend the papal mass and says Croatian president Franjo Tudjman and Moslem chairman of Bosnian collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic will meet soon.

- Bosnia will remain on Europe's conscience for a long time because European policy failed to deliver a decision whether to intervene in the conflict, says former U.N. human rights envoy Tadeusz Mazowiecky.
- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation will get $15 million credit from the World Bank for reconstruction and development of its gas supply system. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
